# Diagnosis: staged RLVR run (nemotron-brorl, turboquant_k2v3_nc, 30 steps)

## Verdict: UNHEALTHY

The run executes to completion without crashes, NaNs, truncation problems or resume drift, but it does not learn: the
training reward never leaves the −1 floor, three of 30 optimizer steps have an exactly-zero gradient, the few updates
that do happen are driven by a single sequence each, and held-out AIME24 accuracy is flat (41/240 at step 8 → 41/240 at
step 30). The learning signal itself is broken by construction.

## Root cause 1 (primary): the new reward function cannot see the model's answers

`math_reward.py` routes every Skywork row to `verl.utils.reward_score.math_dapo.compute_score`. That verifier
(`qat/vendor/verl/verl/utils/reward_score/math_dapo.py:260,166-180`) keeps only the last 300 characters of the response and
accepts an answer only if it matches the Minerva regex `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)`; there is no `\boxed{}` fallback
(`strict_box_verify` defaults to False), and the extracted string must equal the normalized ground truth exactly.
Any response without a literal `Answer:` line is scored `pred="[INVALID]"`, `score=-1`.

The policy, however, is a DeepSeek-R1-distill-style reasoner that terminates with `\boxed{}`, and the training prompts
are the raw Skywork problem text with no format instruction (`evidence/training/*/rollouts/*.gen_001.jsonl`, `input`
field is `<｜User｜>{problem}<｜Assistant｜><think>\n`). Re-scoring the six dumped rollout batches (384 responses) against
the parquet ground truth shows the consequence directly:

| dumped step | has `\boxed{}` | correct by boxed extraction | correct by `math_dapo` (= logged `acc`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 / 4 / 8 / 9 / 20 / 30 | 59 / 56 / 56 / 59 / 62 / 60 of 64 | 12 / 10 / 13 / 14 / 5 / 13 | 1 / 0 / 0 / 1 / 1 / 3 |

Total: 67/384 responses are actually correct, 6/384 are rewarded (+1); 61 correct responses receive −1 and zero cases
go the other way. 53–60 of 64 responses per step are `[INVALID]`. The 6 rewarded responses are precisely those that
happened to also write an `Answer:` line; near-misses such as `'856.'` vs `856` or `'**Finalanswer**'` are rejected by the
exact-string compare. Replicating `math_dapo` on the dumps reproduces the logged `acc` bit-for-bit, so the dumped score is
the quantity that fed the advantages.

Causal chain → observed behaviour:
- `critic/score/mean` sits at −1.0 … −0.875 for all 30 steps (0–4 positives per 64-prompt batch), with no trend.
- Steps 4, 5 and 8 had zero positives → REINFORCE++ global whitening (`core_algos.py:702-734`) of an all-equal return
  gives advantages of exactly 0 → `actor/pg_loss = 0`, `actor/grad_norm = 0` (no parameter change at all on those steps).
- On the other steps, with `rollout.n=1`, `train_batch_size = ppo_mini_batch_size = 64`, `ppo_epochs=1`, one positive
  sample whitened against 63 negatives receives advantage ≈ +9 to +11 (`critic/advantages/abs_max` 8.6–11.2 whenever
  exactly one prompt scored +1; `extreme_count` in the thousands of tokens). Each optimizer step is therefore dominated by
  one sequence, selected by format (`Answer:`) rather than by correctness — a bias toward a format the held-out metric
  does not even measure. Because `bypass_old_logprob_for_rollout=true` with `use_rollout_log_probs=false` puts
  `dp_actor.py` on the on-policy path (`old_log_prob = log_prob.detach()`, "on_policy" printed, `ppo_kl=0`,
  `pg_clipfrac=0`), there is no clipping or importance correction to damp these spikes (`grad_norm` 2.42 at step 22,
  1.10/1.02 at steps 29/30).
- The held-out evaluator (`qat/scripts/eval_math_benchmarks.py:13-16,74`) prepends "put your final answer within
  `\boxed{}`" and grades the last `\boxed{}` with `math_equal`. Train reward and held-out metric thus measure different
  output formats; the train signal is ~90 % false negatives, so there is nothing for the held-out metric to improve on.
  AIME24 (30 × 8 samples, same k2v3 KV cache): E0 31/240 = 12.9 % (base model), E8 41/240 = 17.1 %, E30 41/240 = 17.1 %.
  The 22 steps of the staged phase produce exactly zero held-out change; the +10 at E8 is within sampling noise for 240
  draws and comes from problems the base model already solved (per-problem counts 5→8, 6→5→2, etc.), not from new
  problems.

## Root cause 2 (contributing): the quantized rollout condition produces degenerate samples, so the true signal is sparse

Under `kv_cache_dtype=turboquant_k2v3_nc` (2-bit K / 3-bit V) with `temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=-1` and
`response_length=16384`, 51–58 of 64 training rollouts per step contain >1 % CJK characters (English→Chinese drift,
"的的的" loops, ~9 k tokens mean length). The same pathology appears in the held-out evaluation at temperature 0.7
(21–27 % of samples >1 % CJK, 55–59 % any CJK), so it is a property of the quantized-rollout condition, not something the
training introduced. Its effect is that even a correct verifier would only see ~15 % positives (67/384); combined with
root cause 1 that drops to ~1.5 %.

## Latent defect (connected to observed drift, but not the driver of the flat held-out curve)

The experiment is labelled `ba10.0` and sets `block_align_coef=10.0` (asserted by `run_math_rl.py::check_config`), but
the historical command (`j9073-effective.json`, env index 41 / ray runtime_env index 61) and both phase commands
(`evidence/training/*/native-command.json`) carry `QAT_PROBE_OBJECTIVE=kl`, inherited from the OPD-only job 9073. In
`qat/vendor/verl/verl/workers/actor/dp_actor.py:1716` that env value replaces `policy_loss` with `pg_loss`, so the
block-alignment loss is computed and logged but never back-propagated. Observed confirmation: on steps 4/5/8
`grad_norm` is exactly 0 although `actor/block_align_loss` is 0.076–0.078 — the term contributes no gradient. Without
it, nothing ties the FSDP actor to its quantized-rollout behaviour: `actor/block_align_loss` drifts 0.076 → 0.094–0.097
(steps 29–30) and the rollout/actor log-prob gap widens (`qat/rollout_logprob_mae` 0.36 → 0.44–0.76, bias −0.19 → −0.59,
corr 0.94 → 0.79), while the on-policy REINFORCE path applies no importance correction for that mismatch. This makes the
run a plain (and mis-rewarded) RLVR run rather than the QAT experiment its name claims, but given root cause 1 the
objective would still have had almost no correct signal to optimize.

## Symptoms (not causes)

Flat `critic/score/mean` ≈ −0.97; `[INVALID]` predictions for 83–94 % of rollouts; `pg_loss=0`/`grad_norm=0` on steps
4, 5, 8; single-sample advantage spikes (|A|max ≈ 10) and grad-norm spikes; widening rollout/actor log-prob gap; held-out
AIME24 unchanged between step 8 and step 30.

## Checked and ruled out

- Truncation: train `response_length/clip_ratio` 6–25 %, `aborted_ratio` 0, prompt clip 0 (filter_overlong_prompts at
  512); eval truncation 1/240 at 32 k tokens with 0 extraction failures. Not a factor.
- Resume: phase-2 log shows "Setting global step to 8", lr held at 1.5e-6 (constant after 5 warmup steps), data cursor
  continues (step-9 rows are parquet indices ~513–577 of the unshuffled `data.shuffle=false` order), config diff limited
  to total steps / dirs / `resume_from_path`. Faithful.
- Runtime: no errors or NaNs in either phase log; only benign vLLM warnings (TurboQuant forcing FA2, chunked prefill
  disabled). Checkpoint at step 30 merged and evaluated successfully.
- Data: 16 000 rows, 15 951 after prompt filtering, ground truth stored as JSON lists of strings and parsed correctly by
  `math_reward.py`; no row-level corruption. The defect is in how the answer is extracted from the response, not in the
  labels.

step 30). The learning signal itself is broken by construction.

go the other way. 53–60 of 64 responses per step are `[INVALID]`. The 6 rewarded responses are precisely those that
